subject: Renewal: proposal to stabilize unit pricing via forward commitment
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@cloudscale.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: proposal to stabilize unit pricing via forward commitment

Jordan —

Thanks for taking the quick call earlier. As CloudScale approaches the June 30 renewal, we wanted to propose a structure that locks current unit pricing while giving you runway to forecast and scale without surprise increases. High level: a 36-month forward-commit prepay with an annual ramp schedule and an overage true-up that caps the per-token rate should usage spike.

Why this helps CloudScale:
- Locks in unit economics for 3 years (protects against expected market inflation)
- Provides predictable committed spend to help finance planning
- Includes annual ramp windows (year-by-year consumption bands) so you can start lower and accelerate; unused prepay converts to credits for the next year

Open points we flagged for discussion: the ramp cadence (annual vs. semi-annual), whether you prefer a cash prepay or an invoice schedule, and the acceptable cap on overage rates. I attached a starter SOW + a rate table so you have concrete numbers to react to.

Next step: can you confirm who from procurement should be looped in and if they need a formal PO before we send an updated SOW? If helpful, Marissa can run a 30-minute walkthrough with your finance/procurement team.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Draft_3yr_Prepay_SOW_CloudScale.pdf (pdf)]
[Attachment: Rate_Table_3yr.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@cloudscale.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cloudscale.com
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: proposal to stabilize unit pricing via forward commitment

Alex —

Thanks for the proposal and attachments. A few high-level questions from procurement/finance:

1) Billing: will Redwood accept an annual invoice in advance (preferred) or do you require full 3-yr upfront?
2) Credits/rollover: you mentioned unused prepay converts to credits — what's the expiration and are credits transferable between business units?
3) Overage cap: we need to understand how you define the capped rate and whether there's a true-up schedule (quarterly/annual).
4) Termination/exit: if our usage drops below the first-year band, is there a partial refund mechanism or only credits?

Procurement copied on this thread is Sarah Patel (she's our contracts lead). Please include any standard terms we should expect and a sample invoice cadence.

Jordan
Director of Platform Engineering, CloudScale Inc.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 12:15:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Renewal: proposal to stabilize unit pricing via forward commitment

Looping you both in —

Jordan's procurement questions are standard. Suggested commercial response that we can commit to (pending legal approval):

- Billing cadence: offer annual prepay invoiced at the start of each contract year (option to prepay full 3 years at a 0.75% additional discount)
- Credits/rollover: unused prepay converts to credits that roll into the following contract year; credits expire 12 months after issuance; transferable within the same legal entity only (not between subsidiaries)
- Overage cap: define a capped overage unit rate at 125% of the committed unit price for that year, with quarterly true-ups to reconcile usage vs committed amount
- Termination: allow early termination with a pro-rated refund on unconsumed committed dollars, minus a 10% administrative processing fee; refunds require 90 days notice

I recommend we include an optional "ramp cushion" line item for year 1 (20% buffer) so they don't hit overage immediately as they accelerate. Also: attach the redlined SOW and a pricing appendix.

If you both agree, I'll coordinate with Legal to prepare a 3-year SOW and a short summary memo for procurement.

—Marissa
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redline_SOW_3yr.pdf (pdf)]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 08:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: proposal to stabilize unit pricing via forward commitment

Thanks for the draft commercial terms, Marissa — good starting point. A couple of product/ops considerations we should confirm before sending to CloudScale:

1) Rollover/credits: ensure our billing system can track credit buckets by legal entity and automatically apply them to invoices for year 2. If manual reconciliation is required, include a 60-day reconciliation SLA.
2) Buffer/overage handling: ops has to support the 125% capped rate. Confirm that caching/burst policies won't cause disproportionate cost to Redwood under an aggressive burst scenario. If it does, we should structure a sliding cap (125% first year, 135% second year) tied to usage tiers.
3) Security/contract: verify whether CloudScale needs a SOC2 addendum or audit schedule in the SOW (they asked about protections on prior calls).

If product/ops can sign off, I approve moving forward. Marissa — please ask Legal for the draft SOW and a short schedule that covers billing cadence and reconciliation. Alex — once we have the SOW, can you get procurement's PO contact and target turnaround?

Vivek
VP, Customer Success (acting for renewals approval)

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@cloudscale.com>, procurement@cloudscale.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Renewal: proposal to stabilize unit pricing via forward commitment

Jordan/Sarah —

Appreciate the quick questions. Following internal alignment, here's what we can put on the table for the June renewal: 

1) Billing: annual invoice in advance (yearly prepay) with an optional one-time 0.75% discount for committing to full 36-month payment upfront.
2) Credits: unused prepay converts to credits that roll forward 12 months; credits are scoped to the contracting legal entity and automatically apply to subsequent invoices.
3) Overage: capped overage rate at 125% of the year-specific committed unit price; quarterly true-ups and a usage reconciliation report within 45 days after quarter close. Sliding cap available if you want to increase flexibility in years 2–3.
4) Early termination: pro-rated refund on unconsumed dollars less 10% admin fee and 90 days notice.
5) Security: we'll include SOC 2 attestation reference in the SOW and a clause for audit evidence sharing subject to an NDA.

Next practical steps:
- Marissa will share the redlined SOW and a pricing appendix (attached earlier).
- If procurement can confirm PO process and the contact name, Legal will prepare a 3-year SOW and we can target signature within 3 weeks to lock pricing.

Jordan — if that aligns, can you confirm procurement's PO contact and whether CloudScale prefers annual invoicing or the full upfront option? Once confirmed, I'll route the SOW to Legal.

Thanks —
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Summary_Terms_3yr.pdf (pdf)]
